text: Seabrook Town’s tactical shift to wide, crossing play effectively increased their attacking presence late in the match, as seen in their five final third entries and two shots within eight minutes, creating real pressure despite a tied score of 2-2. Their 3-4-3 formation facilitated wing overloads that compensated for lower possession and pass accuracy compared to Harbour City’s patient short passing. However, the momentum index suggests they struggled to sustain control consistently, highlighting vulnerability in maintaining attacking momentum. Coaching point: emphasize transitions from wide play to quick shots on goal to capitalize more efficiently on created chances during critical match phases.
